newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - "Red hot" market for Globalstar deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - "Red hot" market for Globalstar deal.

text.p: A powerful high-yield market and strengthened credit of Globalstar L.P. led the company back to market six months after it pulled its issue, said Lars Berkman, manager of the $4.2 billion Prudential High Yield Fund Inc.

Berkman cited a litany of factors currently fueling the "red hot" high-yield market, led by the unquenched thirst of insurance companies, pension and mutual funds. Collateralized bond offerings (CBOs) also created demand.
These favorable market conditions were met with the massive equity backing of Globalstar, he said, allowing the company to bring a debt sale twice its original size.

"Globalstar has done a lot of things to make themselves more attractive," Berkman said. "They've raised a lot of money; they've made agreements with telecommunications companies in various countries, which will invest in Globalstar, build local infrastructure to make the system work and agree to market the product."

Globalstar increased the deal from $250 million to $500 million on Thursday before pricing the 2004 senior notes to yield 11.375 percent. The deal included warrants for 1.78 percent of the company, more than the expected 1.0 percent.
The issue is rated B3 by Moody's Investors Service In and single-B by Standard and Poor's.
Lehman Brothers was lead manager on the deal.
While some money managers balked at the deal citing the tight spread and inherent venture risk, Berkman expected the company's backing and profit potential to prevail.

"It's risky," he said. "But the potential in terms of growth and profitability is huge. And the bondholder's $500 million of debt will be senior to $3.8 billion of equity ... It's a huge equity cushion."
Berkman also said guidance of part-owner Loral Space & Communications Ltd bolstered the credit.
